newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end down on EMU uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end down on EMU uncertainties.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed lower on EMU uncertainties, which were aroused again during Wednesday's lackluster session after France's new prime minister named left-wing cabinet appointees, analysts said.
They said there were concerns that the new ministers will carry out campaign pledges to erase record unemployment at the cost of fiscal discipline needed for a single Euro.

Earlier in the day, former European Union president Jacques Delors said he did not believe French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin wanted to water down the so-called "stability pact" to ensure fiscal discipline for the Euro.
Delors also warned against delaying the start date of the single currency.
"The possibility of a delay is greater than a month ago because there are questions of how austere the governments will be," Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist at the Bank of Montreal, said.
"There is the issue that if the Euro is weaker then Germany could delay the start of the launch date," he said.

Some traders were concerned that the German government's plan to revalue its assets at market value and then transfer the profits to meet the budget requirements to join the tEMU would also produce a watered down Euro.
Johnson said reports that the Bundesbank, which objects to the plan, and Bonn were reaching a compromise were non-events, judging from the narrow ranges in the currency market.

June marks edged closer to the GLOBEX low of $0.5771, while June Swiss francs continued to fall through their 3-1/2-week low of $0.6929 on ideas the Swiss National Bank did not want the currency to appreciate on EMU worries.

Overnight SNB president Hans Meyer said that the biggest potential policy problem Switzerland would face in the foreseeable future would be upward pressure on its currency created by uncertainties tied to European monetary union.

However, losses were limited in marks, Swiss francs and yen ahead of Friday's U.S. employment data. The U.S. May National Association of Purchasing Manager's (NAPM) data heightened expectations for a U.S. interest rate hike.
Any signs that the U.S. labor sector remains strong could reinforce ideas that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will raise rates at their next meeting in July.
U.S. weekly jobless claims, which will be released on Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, are expected to fall to 320,000 from 322,000 in the previous week.
Meanwhile, Ford Motor Co said on Wednesday that U.S. auto sales in May fell three percent, capping a second consecutive month of slower industry sales.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000015 at $0.008616, marks fell $0.0013 to $0.5781, Swiss francs lost $0.0051 to $0.6920, sterling was off $0.0026 at $1.6316, Can dollars were down $0.0002 to $0.7278, Aussie dollars were off $0.0032 to $0.7579, and Mexican pesos were $0.000050 to $0.125525.
